definition: Black meets the Queen's Gambit with ...e5, and after dxe5 d4 the advanced d-pawn is a permanent nuisance. Contains one of the most famous traps in chess, the Lasker Trap with its knight underpromotion.
strengths: The d4 pawn cramps White for the whole middlegame
Sharp, and White is often unprepared
weaknesses: A pawn down with compensation that is not always sufficient
Careful play leaves White simply better
caption: The pawn on d4 is the whole idea: it never stops being annoying.

name: Chigorin Defense
definition: Black develops the knight to c6 in front of the c-pawn, breaking a classical rule to fight for the centre with pieces instead of pawns. Unfashionable, fully playable, and unbalanced from move two.
strengths: Unbalanced positions with real winning chances for Black
Off the beaten track: little theory to face
weaknesses: The knight blocks the c-pawn, so ...c5 is unavailable
Black often ends up giving up the bishop pair
caption: Pieces before pawns, and the classical rules deliberately ignored.

name: Semi-Slav Defense
definition: Black plays both ...c6 and ...e6, combining the Slav's solidity with the QGD's flexibility. It leads to the Botvinnik and Moscow variations, among the most analysed positions in all of chess.
strengths: Rock solid, with a genuine plan to win a pawn with ...dxc4 and ...b5
The main lines are theoretically respected at the highest level
weaknesses: The c8 bishop is hard to develop
The Botvinnik Variation requires enormous memorisation
caption: Both pawn moves, both plans, and the sharpest theory in chess.

name: Tarrasch Defense
definition: Black accepts an isolated queen's pawn voluntarily in exchange for free piece play and open lines. Tarrasch insisted activity was worth the weakness; the modern verdict is that he was mostly right.
strengths: Every piece has a natural, active square
Clear plans rather than move-by-move memorisation
weaknesses: The isolated d-pawn is a real weakness in the endgame
White's g3 systems put lasting pressure on d5
caption: An isolated pawn on purpose, for pieces that all have somewhere to go.

name: Bogo-Indian Defense
definition: Black checks on b4 with the bishop against 3.Nf3, aiming for a solid game with fewer forcing lines than the Nimzo. A practical choice for players who want the Nimzo but not its theory.
strengths: Solid and easy to learn
Trades off or repositions the bishop without structural damage
weaknesses: Less ambitious than the Nimzo-Indian
White keeps a small, lasting space advantage
caption: The Nimzo idea against 3.Nf3, with a fraction of the theory.

name: Old Indian Defense
definition: Black plays ...d6 and ...e5 without the King's Indian fianchetto. Solid and cramped, and it usually transposes toward King's Indian structures with the bishop on e7 instead of g7.
strengths: Simple and solid, with a familiar structure
Avoids the vast King's Indian theory
weaknesses: Passive: the bishop on e7 does far less than on g7
White gets an easy space advantage
caption: The King's Indian structure, minus the fianchetto and minus the bite.

name: Torre Attack
definition: White develops Nf3 and Bg5 against a King's Indian or Queen's Indian setup, playing a compact system that works against nearly everything Black tries.
strengths: A system: the same setup against most Black replies
Very little theory for a full opening repertoire
weaknesses: Harmless if Black knows the standard equalising method
The early Bg5 can be met with ...h6 and ...g5 gaining time
caption: One setup, played against almost anything Black does.

name: Colle System
definition: White plays d4, Nf3, e3, Bd3, c3 and prepares a single break with e4. Easy to learn, hard to lose with, and the e4 break can arrive with real force if Black plays too routinely.
strengths: An entire repertoire in five moves, needing no theory
The e3-e4 break generates a genuine kingside attack
weaknesses: The c1 bishop is shut in behind the pawn on e3
Black equalises easily with an early ...Bf5 or ...Bg4
caption: Five setup moves, then one break: e4 arrives with everything behind it.

name: Trompowsky Attack
definition: White plays 2.Bg5 on move two, before Black can choose a defence at all. Every mainstream reply to 1.d4 is sidestepped, which is the entire point.
strengths: Dodges the Nimzo, King's Indian, Grünfeld and Slav in one move
Doubling Black's pawns after Bxf6 gives structural play
weaknesses: The bishop can be chased and lose time
No advantage against a prepared opponent
caption: Move two, and Black's entire prepared repertoire is already gone.

name: Blackmar-Diemer Gambit
definition: White throws in e4 and f3 to sacrifice a pawn for open lines and rapid development against 1.d4 d5. Theoretically dubious and practically dangerous, especially in fast games.
strengths: Wide-open attacking positions and a big development lead
Extremely effective at club level and in blitz
weaknesses: Objectively unsound; strong defence refutes it
Several ways for Black to decline into a comfortable game
caption: A pawn for open lines, and every white piece already out.

name: Stonewall Attack
definition: White builds the pawn wall d4, e3, f4, c3 and attacks on the kingside with Ne5 and a rook lift. Utterly formulaic, which is both its charm and its limit.
strengths: The same plan every game: no theory whatsoever
The e5 outpost and a kingside attack come almost automatically
weaknesses: The e4 square is permanently weak
The c1 bishop is buried behind its own pawns
caption: The wall goes up, the knight lands on e5, and the attack follows.

name: Leningrad Dutch
definition: The Dutch with a kingside fianchetto: ...f5 and ...g6 together. Black gets a King's Indian style attack with the f-pawn already advanced, at the cost of some serious light-square weaknesses.
strengths: Real winning attempts with Black against 1.d4
Combines the Dutch's ...f5 with the King's Indian's bishop
weaknesses: The a2-g8 diagonal and the e6 square are permanently loose
The king's position is airy from the start
caption: ...f5 and ...g6 together: attacking chances, and holes to match.

name: Bird's Opening
definition: 1.f4: a Dutch Defence with an extra tempo. White fights for e5 and plays for a kingside attack, accepting a slightly loose king in exchange.
strengths: A reversed Dutch with a free move
Almost nobody prepares for it
weaknesses: 1.f4 weakens the a7-g1 diagonal at once
From's Gambit gives Black immediate, dangerous play
caption: The Dutch with an extra move, and the same loose king.

name: Nimzo-Larsen Attack
definition: 1.b3, fianchettoing the queen's bishop before anything else. Hypermodern: White lets Black take the centre and attacks it from the flank along the long diagonal.
strengths: Off-theory from move one
The b2 bishop is a genuinely strong long-term piece
weaknesses: Cedes the centre, which a well-prepared opponent will occupy
Slow, and Black can seize space with impunity
caption: The centre is Black's; White plans to undermine it from b2.

name: Modern Defense
definition: Black fianchettoes and gives White the whole centre, planning to attack it later with ...c5 or ...e5. Extremely flexible and transposition-heavy, which suits players who prefer understanding to memorisation.
strengths: Enormously flexible: it transposes into many systems
Very little forced theory to know
weaknesses: Handing over the centre can simply mean being worse
White has several direct, aggressive setups
caption: Take the whole centre; Black intends to attack it later.

name: Nimzowitsch Defense
definition: 1...Nc6, developing a piece toward the centre before committing a pawn. Rare and off-beat, and it leads to positions no opening book has prepared your opponent for.
strengths: Enormous surprise value
Genuinely unbalanced positions from move one
weaknesses: The knight blocks the c-pawn, which Black usually wants to move
White gets a comfortable centre with straightforward play
caption: A knight before a pawn, and no book left to follow.

name: Owen's Defense
definition: 1...b6 and a queenside fianchetto against 1.e4. Hypermodern and rarely seen, aiming pressure at e4 along the long diagonal without committing any pawns.
strengths: Completely off-theory
The b7 bishop pressures e4 from move one
weaknesses: Slow: White can build a big centre unopposed
The unprotected b7 bishop is a tactical liability
caption: Everything aimed at e4 from b7, and not a pawn committed.

name: Benko Gambit
definition: Black sacrifices a wing pawn with ...b5 for lasting pressure down the a- and b-files. The compensation is famously durable: it persists into the endgame, which is unusual for a gambit.
strengths: Compensation that lasts into the endgame, not just the middlegame
Simple, clear plans: rooks on the open queenside files
weaknesses: It is a real pawn, and a well-prepared White can consolidate
Few winning chances if White simply declines
caption: One pawn for two open files, and they never close.

name: King's Indian Sämisch
definition: White plays f3 to bolster e4 and prepare a kingside pawn storm with g4 and h4. The most testing anti-King's-Indian system, and the one that produces the sharpest races.
strengths: Kills Black's usual ...Ng4 counterplay before it starts
Sets up a direct pawn storm with Be3, Qd2 and O-O-O
weaknesses: f3 takes the knight's natural square
Black's ...c5 and ...b5 breaks arrive quickly
caption: f3 first, then the pawns come: the sharpest way to meet the King's Indian.

name: Grünfeld Exchange Variation
definition: White takes on d5 and builds the classic big pawn centre; Black attacks it from the flanks with ...c5, ...Bg7 and pressure on d4. The purest statement of the hypermodern argument.
strengths: An imposing pawn centre and a space advantage
If the centre holds and advances, Black is simply crushed
weaknesses: The centre is a target from move seven onwards
One inaccuracy and the whole structure collapses
caption: A perfect pawn centre, and every black piece aimed at it.
